column1: Cork — the thick bark of the cork oak tree (Quercus suber) - is a remarkable material.
column2: 软木就是栓皮栎（Quercus suber）厚厚的树皮，是一种非同寻常的材料。
column3: the thick bark of the cork oak tree|栓皮栎厚厚的树皮

column1: It is tough, elastic, buoyant, and fire-resistant, and suitable for a wide range of purposes.
column2: 软木坚韧、富有弹性、能浮在水上，还耐火，用途十分广泛。
column7: a wide range of purposes|多种用途

column1: It has also been used for millennia: the ancient Egyptians sealed their sarcophagi (stone coffins) with cork, while the ancient Greeks and Romans used it for anything from beehives to sandals.
column2: 软木已有几千年的使用历史。古埃及人用它密封石棺，古希腊人和古罗马人则用它制作从蜂箱到凉鞋的各种物品。

column1: And the cork oak itself is an extraordinary tree.
column2: 栓皮栎本身也是一种非凡的树。

column1: Its bark grows up to 20 cm in thickness, insulating the tree like a coat wrapped around the trunk and branches and keeping the inside at a constant 20°C all year round.
column2: 它的树皮可厚达20厘米，像一件外套裹住树干和树枝，起到隔热作用，使内部常年保持在20摄氏度。

column1: Developed most probably as a defence against forest fires, the bark of the cork oak has a particular cellular structure - with about 40 million cells per cubic centimetre - that technology has never succeeded in replicating.
column2: 栓皮栎的树皮很可能是为抵御森林火灾而演化形成的，它具有独特的细胞结构。每立方厘米约有4000万个细胞，至今人工技术也没能成功复制这种结构。
column3: as a defence against|用以抵御

column1: The cells are filled with air, which is why cork is so buoyant.
column2: 这些细胞充满空气，因此软木的浮力很强。

column1: It also has an elasticity that means you can squash it and watch it spring back to its original size and shape when you release the pressure.
column2: 软木还有弹性：你可以把它压扁，然后看着它在压力解除后恢复原来的大小和形状。
column6: original size and shape|原来的大小和形状

column1: Cork oaks grow in a number of Mediterranean countries, including Portugal, Spain, Italy, Greece and Morocco.
column2: 栓皮栎生长在多个地中海地区的国家，包括葡萄牙、西班牙、意大利、希腊和摩洛哥。
column4: Mediterranean countries|地中海地区的国家

column1: They flourish in warm, sunny climates where there is a minimum of 400 millimetres of rain per year, and not more than 800 millimetres.
column2: 它们在温暖、阳光充足、年降雨量至少400毫米但不超过800毫米的气候下生长繁茂。

column1: Like grape vines, the trees thrive in poor soil, putting down deep roots in search of moisture and nutrients.
column2: 和葡萄藤一样，栓皮栎也能在贫瘠的土壤里长得十分茂盛。它们向深处扎根，寻找水分和养分。
column6: putting down deep roots|深深扎根

column1: Southern Portugal’s Alentejo region meets all of these requirements, which explains why, by the early 20th century, this region had become the world’s largest producer of cork, and why today it accounts for roughly half of all cork production around the world.
column2: 葡萄牙南部的阿连特茹地区具备上述所有条件。这就解释了为什么到20世纪初，它已成为全球最大的软木产区，也解释了为什么今天该地的软木产量约占全球总产量的一半。
column3: meets all of these requirements|满足上述全部条件
column4: by the early 20th century|到二十世纪初

column1: Most cork forests are family-owned.
column2: 大部分栓皮栎林归家族所有。

column1: Many of these family businesses, and indeed many of the trees themselves, are around 200 years old.
column2: 许多这样的家族企业已有约200年历史；其实，许多树本身也有这么大年纪。

column1: Cork production is, above all, an exercise in patience.
column2: 生产软木，首要的是经得起耐心的考验。
column5: an exercise in patience|一件考验耐心的事

column1: From the planting of a cork sapling to the first harvest takes 25 years, and a gap of approximately a decade must separate harvests from an individual tree.
column2: 从栽下栓皮栎树苗到第一次采剥，需要25年；对同一棵树，两次采剥之间又必须间隔约十年。

column1: And for top-quality cork, it’s necessary to wait a further 15 or 20 years.
column2: 想得到最高品质的软木，还必须再等15年或20年。

column1: You even have to wait for the right kind of summer’s day to harvest cork.
column2: 就连采剥的日子也得挑，要等到夏天气候合适的那一天。

column1: If the bark is stripped on a day when it’s too cold - or when the air is damp — the tree will be damaged.
column2: 如果在天气太冷或空气潮湿的时候剥皮，树就会受损。

column1: Cork harvesting is a very specialised profession.
column2: 采剥软木是一门专业性很强的行当。

column1: No mechanical means of stripping cork bark has been invented, so the job is done by teams of highly skilled workers.
column2: 至今仍未有人发明用机械剥取软木树皮的办法，因此这项工作由技艺娴熟的工人组队完成。
column6: highly skilled workers|技艺娴熟的工人

column1: First, they make vertical cuts down the bark using small sharp axes, then lever it away in pieces as large as they can manage.
column2: 工人先用锋利的小斧沿树皮纵向劈开切口，再把树皮一块块撬下来，尽可能保留大块。
column7: as large as they can manage|在力所能及的范围内尽量大

column1: The most skilful cork-strippers prise away a semi-circular husk that runs the length of the trunk from just above ground level to the first branches.
column2: 最熟练的剥皮工能撬下一整片半圆筒形的树皮，长度从略高于地面的树干底部一直延伸到第一层树枝。
column7: runs the length of|沿……全长延伸

column1: It is then dried on the ground for about four months, before being taken to factories, where it is boiled to kill any insects that might remain in the cork.
column2: 剥下的树皮先在地上晾晒约四个月，再送到工厂煮沸，杀死可能残留在软木中的昆虫。

column1: Over 60% of cork then goes on to be made into traditional bottle stoppers, with most of the remainder being used in the construction trade.
column2: 之后，超过60%的软木被加工成传统瓶塞，其余的大部分用于建筑业。

column1: Corkboard and cork tiles are ideal for thermal and acoustic insulation, while granules of cork are used in the manufacture of concrete.
column2: 软木板和软木砖是理想的隔热、隔音材料，软木颗粒则用于制造混凝土。
column5: thermal and acoustic insulation|隔热和隔音

column1: Recent years have seen the end of the virtual monopoly of cork as the material for bottle stoppers, due to concerns about the effect it may have on the contents of the bottle.
column2: 近些年来，软木作为瓶塞材料近乎垄断市场的局面已经结束，原因是人们担心它可能影响瓶内盛装的产品。
column8: contents of the bottle|瓶内所装的产品

column1: This is caused by a chemical compound called 2,4,6-trichloroanisole (TCA), which forms through the interaction of plant phenols, chlorine and mould.
column2: 这种影响来自一种名为2,4,6-三氯苯甲醚（TCA）的化合物。它是植物酚类物质、氯和霉菌相互作用的产物。

column1: The tiniest concentrations — as little as three or four parts to a trillion - can spoil the taste of the product contained in the bottle.
column2: 即使浓度极低，低至万亿分之三或四，这种物质也足以败坏瓶中产品的味道。
column5: three or four parts to a trillion|万亿分之三或四

column1: The result has been a gradual yet steady move first towards plastic stoppers and, more recently, to aluminium screw caps.
column2: 于是，市场缓慢而持续地转向替代品，起初转向塑料瓶塞，近些年来则转向铝制螺旋盖。
column3: gradual yet steady|渐进但持续的

column1: These substitutes are cheaper to manufacture and, in the case of screw caps, more convenient for the user.
column2: 这些替代品的制造成本更低；就螺旋盖而言，使用起来也更方便。
column4: cheaper to manufacture|制造成本较低

column1: The classic cork stopper does have several advantages, however.
column2: 不过，经典的软木瓶塞确实有几项优势。

column1: Firstly, its traditional image is more in keeping with that of the type of high quality goods with which it has long been associated.
column2: 首先，软木瓶塞的传统形象，更符合那些长期以来与它联系在一起的优质商品的形象。

column1: Secondly — and very importantly — cork is a sustainable product that can be recycled without difficulty.
column2: 其次，而且非常重要的是，软木是一种可持续利用、又容易回收的产品。
column5: sustainable product|可持续利用的产品

column1: Moreover, cork forests are a resource which support local biodiversity, and prevent desertification in the regions where they are planted.
column2: 再者，栓皮栎林有助于维持当地的生物多样性，还可防止种植地发生荒漠化。

column1: So, given the current concerns about environmental issues, the future of this ancient material once again looks promising.
column2: 因此，鉴于当下人们对环境问题的关切，这种古老材料的前景再一次显得颇有希望。
